title: Black Rhinos in the Ngorongoro Crater
excerpt: The Ngorongoro Crater is one of the best places in Tanzania to see a black rhino. Why they live there and how to spot them.
body:
Black rhinos are critically endangered, and seeing one in the wild is special. The Ngorongoro Crater is one of the most reliable places in Tanzania to do so.

## Why the crater works

The crater's floor is open, so rhinos can be spotted from a distance, and its natural walls help protection. Rangers monitor the population closely.

## How many?

The crater's population is small, in the tens rather than hundreds. Exact numbers are kept vague for security reasons.

## How to spot them

- Rhinos often stay far from the roads. Binoculars and a guide with sharp eyes help.
- Early morning is best.
- They are often seen in open grassland or near the Lerai forest.

## Black vs white rhino

The rhinos in Tanzania are black rhinos. They have a hooked lip for browsing on shrubs and are more solitary than white rhinos. See [rhino facts](/blog/rhino-facts/).

## Other places

Rhinos are also present in parts of the Serengeti and in [Mkomazi](/blog/mkomazi-rhino-sanctuary/).

## Help conservation

Park fees help fund protection. Follow your guide's instructions and never share exact locations of rhinos on social media.
